decision: WF-128 picks one SFU and one deck engine for an in-room live presentation, with the licence and the reason recorded

state.constraint: No realtime transport exists in this product. The workflow is modelled as pure rules, roles and an event log; the live link and the recording are stand-ins.

sfu.LiveKit: Apache-2.0, egress for compositing/recording/transcoding to HLS
sfu.BigBlueButton: LGPL-3.0, purpose-built for presentation and recording
sfu.mediasoup: ISC, a custom SFU library with no egress

deck.Slidev: MIT, needs a Node build step per deck

state.data_flow: Presenter screen/audio -> SFU (selective forwarding) -> per-participant tiles; recording composed via egress -> HLS/MP4 -> stored with the room
state.issue_instruction: Pick one SFU, record the licence you picked and why, and put the decision in the technical design doc. Do not build against all four.

sfu.instructions: Which single SFU best matches this workflow's researched data flow ('recording composed via egress -> HLS/MP4'), given that the build installs none of them and only records the choice?

criteria.LiveKit: Apache-2.0 permissive licence, and its egress component is the recording path the data flow names
criteria.Jitsi Meet: Apache-2.0, but recording is an add-on rather than a first-class egress
criteria.BigBlueButton: Purpose-built for presentation and recording, but LGPL-3.0 copyleft and a heavier deployment
criteria.mediasoup: ISC, but a library with no egress, so the whole recording path would be custom work

deck.instructions: Which single presentation engine best matches the rule this workflow enforces ('a reveal order is respected'), given that the room's own pages stand in for the deck?

criteria.reveal.js: MIT, and its fragment model is exactly a reveal-per-step order, so rule and engine agree
criteria.Slidev: MIT, but it needs a Node build step per deck, which does not fit a room's stored pages
criteria.impress.js: MIT, but unmaintained and its model is spatial rather than an ordered reveal

confident.instructions: Is the evidence strong enough to pick one of each decisively rather than deferring?

criteria.true: One candidate is clearly better on the stated criteria
criteria.false: The candidates are close or the criteria are under-specified

decision: WF-128 resolves the research's own disagreement about where attendance and questions are written

product_facts.crm_write_back: No CRM connector is provisioned for this feature; other workflows own CRM sync.
product_facts.deal_surface_that_exists: The room record, which is the deal's surface in this product.
product_facts.questions: The user flow says 'questions asked live are logged against the deal'.

candidate_readings.room_record: Write attendance and questions to the room record; declare the CRM write-back as a gap.
candidate_readings.crm_only: Write to a CRM surface the product does not provision, and leave the room without the data.
candidate_readings.both: Write to the room record and also attempt a CRM write the build cannot make.

destination.instructions: Which destination should attendance and questions be written to, given the two research lines disagree and only one surface exists in this product?

criteria.room_record: Writes to a surface that exists, keeps the data with the deal, and declares the CRM gap honestly
criteria.crm_only: Follows the automation line but leaves the room with no attendance, because no CRM write-back exists here
criteria.both: Writes to the room and also claims a CRM write the build does not make

decision: Implementation of WF-128 meets the release bar

state.change_summary: WF-128 adds an in-room live presentation / co-browsing workflow as new files only: the domain package backend/dsr/live_sessions/ (vocabulary, errors, pure rules and one engine that reads and writes through RecordStore alone), the feature module owning /api/wf-128 with a seed hook, 78 backend tests in two files, a frontend page in frontend/src/features/wf-128-live-presentation/ with 11 tests, and the technical design doc the issue requires. No shared file is edited. The research's live transport does not exist in this product, so the session is modelled as state, roles and an event log; a follower polls a read-only state route and acknowledges on a write sync route, so every write's audit row names a route the app serves. The issue's required stack decision is recorded with licence and reason (LiveKit Apache-2.0, reveal.js MIT) and the attendance/CRM disagreement is resolved to the room record, both settled by Jev.

declared_unverified: No realtime transport exists in this product. The live link, the SFU, the deck engine and the recording artefact reference are stand-ins by design, and the vocabulary and the page say so.

No recorder, no media hosting and no CRM write-back are built. Auto-translate captions and auto-clip highlights are named and not built. Per-participant link gating is owned by the existing link-gating and revocation workflows and is not enforced here.
The local whole backend suite is not fully green: one pre-existing order/contention flake (a 300 second seeder subprocess timeout) failed under a 37 minute loaded run and passed alone. CI is green.

The local whole frontend suite is not fully green: two runs failed one to two files each and the failing files differed between runs (wf-086 once, wf-029 once). Both pass alone (20 and 22 tests), neither is owned by this change, and the latest CI run on origin/main is green.

tools/verify_all_routes.py and tools/verify_localhost.py ran against a server started in-process (this host reaps a child server process mid-request) rather than as a detached background process; both still spoke real HTTP to 127.0.0.1:8000.

I did not comment on issue #138 because this run forbids posting to external channels. The attendance/CRM destination decision the issue asked be recorded in a comment is recorded in docs/workflows/WF-128-TECHNICAL-DESIGN.md and in the pull request body instead.
state.requirements: A feature adds files and edits no shared file. All reads and writes go through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase so every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The feature owns a unique route prefix with no colliding concrete (method, path) pair. Tests exist and the whole suite is green. The frontend page builds, is discovered by the glob, and meets the design floor.

contract_compliance.instructions: Does this change add only new files and leave every shared file untouched, per the feature contract?

criteria.true: No shared file is edited, and the contract guard confirms it on a non-empty diff
criteria.false: A shared file is edited, or the guard did not actually measure a diff

claims_backed_by_measurement.instructions: Is every claim made in the evidence supported by a measurement that was actually run, rather than asserted, read off a progress bar, or produced by a check that passed on empty input? Declared limits are not a failure of this question -- they are the honest disclosure that belongs to them.

criteria.true: Each claim traces to quoted, reproducible tool output
criteria.false: A claim is asserted, or a check passed vacuously or was not run

coverage_of_the_change.instructions: Setting aside what is declared unverified, how much of the change did the evidence actually exercise? Judge breadth, not honesty: a declared limit is fine, but a large unexamined surface is not.

criteria.true: Every surface the change introduces is exercised by a measurement, with at most incidental limits declared
criteria.false: A substantial part of the change was never measured, whether or not that is declared

audit_integrity.instructions: Does this change preserve the audited-store guarantee: all writes through the wrapper, no direct database connection, no schema change outside the envelope?

criteria.true: Writes go through the audited store and the envelope is unchanged
criteria.false: A direct connection is opened, or a typed column or migration is added

design_floor.instructions: Does the frontend meet the design floor -- 44px touch targets, visible focus, a text label beside every icon, no emoji as icons, reduced motion respected -- as checked by the scripted pass?

criteria.true: The scripted design-floor pass is green
criteria.false: The pass is red, was skipped, or is on the allowlist

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.

criteria.merge: Evidence supports landing it: suite green, contract intact, floor met
